summary: A memo by John McCarthy on how documents with arbitrary characters could be stored, shown, edited and printed on any equipment. It reviews where things stood: 96-character ASCII, many sites on 64-character sets, and Stanford's larger character set. It then proposes how to move toward a larger shared set, with special reference to the ARPANET.

eli5.summary: Different computers know different letters, so some cannot show certain symbols. This note asks how all machines could share a bigger alphabet so everyone can read each other's documents.
